title: Bill Green, the multi-reed studio musician
summary: They discuss Green's mastery of all reeds, his lack of recognition outside studios, and his teaching in Kansas City.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yes, it was. It was very good. Bill Green is someone who is certainly deserving of wider recognition.
Yes, he is. He can do it all. Did you ever see him play his bassoon riding a unicycle.
A unicycle? Yes.
Oh, you've seen it. [LAUGHS]
Well, my daughter studied flute with him. Bill used to give us demonstrations. Karate demonstrations, unicycle demonstrations, and we heard him on all the instruments.
He plays all of the reeds equally well. Alto saxophone, tenor, baritone, oboe, bassoon, English horn. He's a marvel.
He really is. And unfortunately, he's not well known away from the studio scene on the West Coast.
Well, that's the problem with the studios. Unless you have nerve enough to get out of the studios and let people know what you do, they'll never know who you are.
His name is not known at all, I don't think, away from here.
No. Well, he hasn't made any records.
He's on a lot.
He's on a lot of records, but not under his own name. And now... You've probably heard the same program I did. He did Coleman Hawkins' version of "Body and Soul."
Yes.

And he does a lot of Charlie Parker originals with the reeds... Well, he does them with different combinations. George Bohannon playing trombone... I think maybe he should do a record on his own, with some new material. I'm not against what he's doing, but I think some new material that would be fresh to people. Because he is a truly marvelous musician.
Yes, he certainly is. And he's been a part of many important bands, as well as recording sessions and soundtracks. He's currently, I believe, playing with Nat Pierce-Randy Capp's Juggernaut.
Oh, is he doing that? He probably is.
I think he just played the Concord Festival with them, and a festival in Oregon. I've seen him in many of the local bands. But he never travels. He never leaves home. Right?

He leaves home, but only... His home is in Kansas City. When he goes, he just goes on a vacation. But he never takes a band out on the road. He's so busy with his students, you know... He's a professional teacher besides being one of the ace studio musicians.
